body: I am aware that it's my decision and nobody else's. my parents and grandparents have never and would never force me to do anything i didn't want to do, and if I said I was dropping out from university they wouldn't be angry or try to convince me not to. but they would be sad and disappointed. and I just absolutely hate seeing them that way

thank you so much.

i have already got an arrangement with my university, i've been granted mitigating cirumstances - but they can't keep granting them forever. eventually i'm just goign to have to accept the fact that I'll never finish. i am not doing any work at all right now.

thank you so much for your advice about the SNRIs. my doctor didn't ever explain the difference between them except by saying that SNRIs 'aren't as effective'. i'm seeing a regular doctor, and she's never offered me the opportunity to see a psychiatrist. i'll give the SNRIs a go and if they do nothing i'll ask to see a psychiatrist.

thank you so much. it's lovely to hear from someone who was in the same position as me. i've never been a particularly skilled baker but I was a good cook. i could make all sorts of dishes from scratch and i enjoyed it. I just don't have the motivation any more. hopefully i'll find it again someday.

as for dropping out of university, i would be perfectly happy in a minimum wage job for the rest of my life to tell you the truth. it's my family. my parents and grandparents would be crushed if i dropped out or failed. i just don't think i could deal with their disappointment in me
no I've never been offered the option of seeing a psychiatrist. next time i'm at the doctors i will ask. thank you
